newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission set to discuss media directive.
newsitem.headline: Commission set to discuss media directive.

text.p: The European Commission will re-examine next Wednesday the draft media concentration directive.

The plan the Commission will consider at its weekly meeting -- focused on protecting the single market and guaranteeing media pluralism -- would stop companies extending their control of a country's television and radio stations once their audience share reaches a certain level.

According to a document made available to Reuters the ceiling has been set at 30 percent for owners operating in only one field, whether it be television or radio, and an average of 10 percent per medium for those operating in several areas, including the written press.

The plans -- drawn up in response to a demand from the European Parliament for a brake on over-concentration in the interests of democracy -- were put on the backburner last September after failing to muster sufficient support from the 20 Commissioners.
They will re-emerge almost unchanged and have a good chance of approval this time round, EU officials said.
In the run-up to the meeting European publishers were conducting a frenzied lobbying effort to prevent the plan being agreed.
The European Publishers Council described the plan as "onerous legislation on an industry fighting to compete in the information society."
The publishers say that the goal would be better served by use of the EU's existing competition rules.

"In our view the convergence of traditional media with new forms of delivery, leading to lowered barriers of entry and greater consumer choice of media sources, means that media specific legislation is entirely unnecessary," Sir Frank Rogers, the Council's Chairman said in a statement.
